utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My usual appeal to you. If there are problems with interpretation, please let me know straight away. Defence teams seem to be in full force minus Mr. Bourgon, conspicuously absent. The Prosecution is minus Julian Nicholls and Mr. van der Puye, if I am pronouncing his name well. I take it once the witness is already in the courtroom that there are no preliminaries? That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We hope to finish today and then you can go home to your work. So who is next? Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Lazarevic is lead counsel for Borovcanin, accused Borovcanin. Mr. Lazarevic, he's all yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, in response to questions by Mr. McCloskey during the examination-in-chief, when you were shown the footage which is Prosecution Exhibit 2103, you said that there was some markings on some of those aerial shots, whether by you or by your colleagues. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what footage you are meaning when you talk about the exhibit 2103. I would need to see it, if it is in relation to this one, that I indeed did some markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for drawing my attention to that. We're going to come to the specific shot. What I'm interested in is the methodology you used when you made the markings. Actually, my next question would be: When you were making these markings, whether this was done by you or your colleagues from the Prosecutor's office, were you guided by information that you received from witnesses whom you were interviewing in the course of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer would be yes and no, because to mark the bus company Ekspres on the aerial imagery of Potocari didn't really need witnesses. We have been enough times to this place to know what the buildings are and be able to pinpoint them on an aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We will look at the specific photograph that I'm interested in and then you can answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown photograph number 6 from the set of photographs which bear number P2103.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recall this photograph, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony on the 7th of September, 2006 - and this is transcript page 1319, from line 25 to line 12 on 1320 - you said that this yellow square marking one of the buildings marked by the words "UN Base," you said that this was the area where the refugees were. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this is the UN base in which 5.000 among a total of 25.000 refugees were taking shelter. The other ones are in an area that I have shown on another photograph. But on this one, it is all the area Ekspres bus compound and Energoinvest, zinc factory. This is the broad perimeter where the other refugees took shelter. I think this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Similar. However, you also said that the Feros facility that we can see on the photograph here and in another building, which was -- is marked here as the Blue Factory, you said that the refugees were not located here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you one thing: This yellow rectangle that we see on this photograph, did you draw that in or did one of your colleagues do that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this specific picture my answer was that I did not recall if I did this marking - that was done in preparation for the trial of General Krstic - or if another colleague did it. I would think that it was another one because I would not have personally put an arrow on the electrical station, because it is not a reference point for the investigation in this area. So I think it has been done by someone else. But I confirm the markings for all what is on this photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's not really of the utmost importance, whether you marked this or whether one of your colleagues did, but I'm interested in what you said in reference to the Feros building, the Blue Factory. I assume that what you said is based on witness statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume that these were witnesses who were in Potocari between the 11th and the 13th of July, 1995; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Amongst the people who were in Potocari at the time, there was a witness. Do you have the list of witnesses here indicated by numbers? I do not want to mention the name of this witness. Perhaps if you can just look. This is a list you had with you during your testimony, and if you would kindly look at number 42, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak with this witness? Did you take a statement from him?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said once, there are two survivors of Branjevo farm, a young one and an old one, and I took a statement of the young one -- the younger one. But I don't know if -- which one of the two is the one I'm talking about. We already had that little problem, but you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about witness marked 42. My question was whether you spoke with witness marked here as number 42. Did you take a statement from him? Did you perhaps show him some photographs? Did you have any contact with this witness marked by number 42?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have exactly the same answer. If I cannot identify number 42 as being the young one, and you know who is the old one because he was here some short time ago, so you just need to tell me if he's the young one. Then my answer will be yes. If not, it will be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's the older one. So your position is that you did not take the statement from Witness 42, the older one who testified here some time ago before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me a recollection that is now 11 years old. And if I took the statement, my name and signature is on it, and I'm sure you have it in your records. So if my name is on it, no doubt I took a statement from him, yes. If not, I didn't; another colleague did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that you couldn't recall whether you did or didn't, that would then be your answer, in brief; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we move to private session for just a very brief period? I want to make sure not to disclose the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Number 42, you can disclose his name because he testified in open session. So we have no problem then. Or I can tell you that just -- while following you, of course, I was checking other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was just trying to be careful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. You can't refer to the other one. But Witness 42, you can definitely refer to by name. Do you still want to go into private session or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll remain in public session and we will proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a part of the transcript from the testimony of Witness 42 in these proceedings on the 6th of September of this year. I would like to quote page 1231 of the transcript, lines 20 to 24. It begins like this: [In English] "The people were in a number of buildings. I do not know exactly how many, but perhaps there were five or six of these buildings, factories that are there. There is the lead factory, the Zinc Factory, Akumulator, Feros, perhaps some other ones. There's some other factories." [Interpretation] After that, again on page 1232 of the transcript of the same day, line 11, this witness states: [In English] "The people were being placed in these buildings, in these factories. They are quite close to each other. Some are above the road; some are below the road. Maybe they are 50 to 60 metres apart, up to 100 metres, depending on the factory. And there were people again in between the factories because you could not fit 30.000 people into the buildings, all of them. That is quite clear." [Interpretation] So now you've heard this part of the testimony of Witness 42, and it's evident on the basis of it that they were also in the buildings which were close to the UN base, the Feros, the Blue Factory, and in the area between them. So not only in the area that was marked on photograph number 6.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have a clue how you are drafting this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you like, I can read this part of the transcript again. But the witness was recently heard before this Trial Chamber and he was questioned in detail about the area where they were in Potocari as refugees, and he stated here that they were in the area between the UN base, also in these other buildings that are very close to it. That's how I reached my conclusion. But, actually, my question to you is whether this testimony as it is would make you, perhaps, change your position regarding the places where the refugees were from the 11th to the 13th of July, in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two elements in my answer. The first one is that I -- the witness gives a perfectly accurate description of the situation. He absolutely nowhere points to the fact that the Blue Factory, the so-called Blue Factory, in between the area of all the factories he's naming and the UN base, was used by refugees. The investigation concludes from the testimonies of others that this place was sealed off and not accessible. This can also be seen from aerial imagery that the line of refugees is beyond, anyhow, this factory as an additional element. So the second point is I absolutely don't change my conclusion regarding the fact that the so-called Blue Factory was not accessible to the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question. You will agree, of course, that Witness 42, who was there at the time - there's no doubt about that - knows certainly very well where he was and where the other refugees were located?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. This is why I personally don't see in his declaration what gives you the certainty that the Blue Factory, so-called Blue Factory, was used by the refugees. But I need also to add that it doesn't seem to me extremely relevant to know if it was used by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Ruez. It would be good if you answered more briefly. Otherwise, the time that I allotted for this cross-examination would have to be extended. So I would like to cover the material a little bit more quickly. So I would appreciate it very much if you would just answer briefly the questions I put to you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't hesitate to take your time. I have all my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You seem to be in agreement because you have enough time, Mr. Ruez. It's true that when you testified back on the 7th of -- because I'm just checking it, on the 7th of September, you were categoric as regards the Blue Factory, saying that the Blue Factory was sealed off, cordoned off, by the Bosnian Serb army and there were no refugees in it. But you also included the Feros in the same category. If you -- I want to correct that and you need to do that. Let me read to you what you said at page 1320, line 6: "As we go down, as the Blue Factory, so-called Blue Factory, in front of it, alongside of the road, a building named from its company Feros." "And then any particular significance from the investigation of those two buildings?" That was the question. Your answer: "We -- as far as we know, these ones were not used as a shelter by the refugees. This area had been cordoned off by the Bosnian Serb army." And then you started referring to the White House. So when you testified, you put in the same basket both the Blue Factory and the Feros Factory. Now, Witness 42 -- Witness 42 -- now, let me see how I'm going to do this. How do I collapse this again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I read from yours? Now, Witness 42, according to Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if you would kindly do that, please. Specifically, it refers to Feros. He does not mention the Blue Factory as such, but he does mention Feros Factory as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In answer to the question put by Stojanovic, which says: "Since we are familiar with the layout, can you please tell us whether you're talking about one building or several buildings where the people were?" The answer was, line 20: "The people were in large -- in a number of buildings. I don't know exactly how many, but perhaps there were five or six of these buildings, factories that are there. There is the lead factory, the zinc factory, Akumulator, Feros, perhaps some other ones. There were some other factories." Is this the passage you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And later on, Judge Kwon --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can help. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6, Mr. Lazarevic is reading, of course, in English. "After that the witness had mentioned indeed the Feros. He mentioned the lead factory, the Zinc Factory, Akumulator, Feros, perhaps some other ones." Now, I take it none of these would be the Blue Factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two things also in this. Indeed Feros is a building. The admin building of the Feros company is just adjacent to the so-called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's opposite.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just next to it. They make, let's say, like one block, though they are two buildings. I point out that the witness is saying what the situation was, so people in all the factories, and he's listing, for the sake of the purpose, all the factories he knows in the area. But I do not see that it was pointed out to him: Do you know whether Feros was used. Again, I repeat, our information is from several witness accounts that the Blue Factory was not used by the refugees. It was sealed off. Their assumption was that it was used as a base for the army. We did not particularly investigate this. We know that the line of refugees were during July 12 at the level of the access on the road to the Ekspres compound, that it moved a bit in the direction north of about 50 metres during the day of the July 13. The area of this Blue Factory, with "Feros" next to it is, let's say, one more -- at least one more, 50 metres towards the direction of the UN compound. And there were -- there were no refugees in this -- in this precise location. But would there be some? Again, I don't really see the point. We have investigated this place. We have no reports of crimes committed there. We didn't even search inside it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's make it clear. Insofar as this Witness 42 may have hinted in his testimony that included in the buildings where the refugees were quartered were also the Blue Factory and Feros Factory, he's wrong. You wouldn't agree with him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Luckily he didn't mention the Blue Factory. But in respect of Feros, I have to say also that I didn't show the photograph, but when you are sitting on the balcony of the White House, the building you have just in front of your eyes is Feros.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ruez, I would like to move to a different topic now. Let us watch one video clip that we had occasion to see on the first day of your evidence here. If I understand it correctly, this is a compilation of several footages. Could we just review some parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the Trial Chamber and my learned colleagues from the Prosecution, it's video footage V000-4458, and it bears 65 ter number of the Prosecution exhibit list 1577. And we'll take a look for only some very short sequence of this -- sequences of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the part of the video that I wanted to see. Okay. I believe we can stop now. For the record, the part that was played starts with 03:00 and lasts to 03:17.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ruez, the soldiers we see here on this still, can you confirm to me that these are indeed UN soldiers? If you want me to, I can have the tape played again.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No need to play it again. The still is good enough. They are wearing blue helmets, so the assumption is indeed they are UN troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please continue watching the video clips. This is the same video clip, but we will look at a different sequence of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back a bit. That is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the two soldiers carrying weapons? This is taking place in Srebrenica. Can you confirm that these two soldiers are also members of the United Nations forces?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This picture is taken at the Bravo Company in Srebrenica town, and the two soldiers in that location are definitely members of the DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we will take a brief look at another part of the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that we are viewing this particular part, sir -- can we please stop there. Mr. Ruez, do you see the man pointing with his arm? And we saw the text saying that he was addressing the crowd, saying that the road ought to be blocked. Do you see the man?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise him, perhaps, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know what he's doing at this moment, but I don't know his name or who he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name -- by the name of Nesib Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I absolutely know the name Nesib Mandzic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to speak to Nesib Mandzic, to see him in person?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps recognise him at this still?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stop there briefly? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are these UN soldiers? Or, rather, the soldier we can see in the middle of the footage here.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's a UN soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the three soldiers, too?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The three soldiers, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us see a bit more of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these are also UN soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the people wearing blue helmets and camouflage uniform on this footage are, yes, UN soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, we stopped at 08:36.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you have now seen several stills where you identified soldiers as UN soldiers. Tell me, is it fair to say that all these stills where we saw UN soldiers, we were able to see that all of them wore camouflage flak jackets?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it also fair to say that none of the UN soldiers we saw had light blue flak jackets? They all had camouflage flak jackets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is what I wanted to show you in the video footages. I would like to move on now. On the 7th of September, 2006, during your evidence here, while the discussion concerned the so-called Petrovic video footage, 1320, lines 2 to 9, you said at that point that Petrovic's footage, which contained a sequence with Kravica and the White House was something that you received from your friend, a Dutch journalist. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I have no friend who is a Dutch journalist. What I said is that I saw it for the first time when a Dutch journalist came to visit me in order to show me these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood your testimony. Maybe it was due to misinterpretation. What was it precisely that you saw? Did he show this to you without handing it over to you, or did this Dutch journalist actually hand the tape containing the footage over to you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not handed over the tape. I was shown the pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me - of course if you recall - when this was precisely? You did not tell us exactly when it was, which year, which month. Perhaps the date.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I hardly remember, but it would be easy to find because it was a very short time before the OTP had access to the tape, or at least before I learned that the OTP also had had access to the tape. It's the same year and most probably around the same month. But I don't recall when that was. I was on my island in the Caribes, so it was after 2001, that's for sure. Maybe 2002, at the end of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the Dutch journalist who showed you the footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two of them, and I have no recollection of their names, nor even of -- for what -- they were working for TV, but I don't even know where -- I don't remember which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Once you were shown the footage by these two journalists or, rather, at the time you were shown the footage by them, you did not work for the OTP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had left the Tribunal in April, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you do after you saw the footage? Did you tell the journalists to notify the OTP of the existence of the footage, or did you yourself inform the OTP about the footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is when I informed that I learnt that the OTP also had recently had access to these pictures, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, when you got in touch with the OTP, the existence of the footage was no longer a surprise for them. They were already in possession of it.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you tell us who it was you got in touch with from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Peter McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So naturally he was the one to tell you that they already had the footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was disappointed I didn't bring him hot news. He already had the thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he got it from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There's such a thing as -- I don't think you should have asked that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I would like us to address a different subject now which has to do with your investigation concerning Srebrenica and certain procedures you went through during your investigation. One of the issues which came up during the investigation process was the seizing of various documentation from the army and elsewhere. Did you take part in these actions of seizing documentation and such like?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will put very specific questions to you now which will have to do with specific locations where these seizures to place, and I wish you to tell me whether you, as the chief investigator, took part in them or not. So I only need a yes or no answer from you. The public security station or centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The public security centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in the searching and seizing of the MUP archives of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me put another question to you. Did you take part in the searching and seizing of the documentation by the Special Police Brigade of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you did take part in some other seizing actions, what was the procedure like of seizing documentation? I suppose you, together with investigators, enter certain premises and then you proceed to seize documentation. At that point, do you make a record of the documentation you seize? I mean -- and I'm referring to those centres or seizing actions where you took part.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took part in two search and seizure operations. The first one was in the summer of 1996. It was a search and seizure in a container at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters in which we seized a certain number of blue helmets that had been taken from the Dutch Battalion at that time. The second operation was the search and seizure at the Bratunac Brigade. That was simultaneous, as you know, to the same operation conducted at the Zvornik Brigade. So at the Zvornik Brigade, the material seized was listed on a log. Only one specific situation was the search of the office of the security officer, Mr. Lazar Ostojic, lieutenant or captain at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think, just to get the record straight, I think we're getting the brigades -- he said Zvornik, and I think he means the other brigade. Just to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. At the Zvornik Brigade it was the same procedure. It was the logging of the material. The only exception to that is at the Bratunac Brigade, the office of the security officer, since at one point I conducted the search and seizure personally, I did it in what I call the French way, that is we brought down a detailed list with a description of all the documents seized in that office. So that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was precisely what I was interested in, the procedure. You describe it, that this was the French way, but was it in general the procedure applied by the OTP in seizing documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you answer that question? Because if you don't know, please don't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot answer. I can only answer for the operations that I took part into. And the way the things were done was to have the document -- I mean, to have all the material logged and signed by a representative of those who are taking the material away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's precisely what I'm interested in. A list of documents seized is drafted, which list is then presented to the representative of the organisation on whose premises the seizure was carried out, and they do confirm that this was in fact the documentation that was seized by you from their premises. Is that the procedure?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My next question will perhaps call for a somewhat hypothetical answer on your part. In order to seize the documentation of the Special Police Brigade, all the documents seized would be listed and the representative of the organisation would have to put his signature down confirming that they were in fact handed over to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness has said he wasn't involved in any of those searches, so this is not just hypothetical, it would be extremely speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the question itself premised it would be a somewhat hypothetical answer. So let's go to the next question, unless you're familiar with the events relating the events you're being asked about, in which case you're free to answer. But please do not speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not speculate. I was not at the Tribunal any longer when that search occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ruez. Mr. Lazarevic, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have just a few more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already asked you about the centres in Zvornik, Bijeljina, and these others. You said that you did not take part in them. But can I ask you the following: Do you know who did take part in it? And, of course, I'm asking you about the OTP investigators.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was waiting for the translation delay. Sorry. No, I don't know who took part in these other searches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions. However, I would like to retain the right to, well, ask this witness again when he comes back in the presence of the attorneys of the US embassy regarding aerial images. I would like to retain the right to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Lazarevic. I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Ms. Fauveau. Ms. Fauveau is appearing for General Miletic. Now, Madam Fauveau will be firing her questions in French, which is your native tongue. So please, I exhort you both to allow a small pause between question and answer, even though I assume that you will be answering in English. But allow a brief interval of time. Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I'd like to clarify one point concerning Bratunac. On several occasions you said that in Bratunac there was the old school and Karadzic school. Can you confirm that there were, in effect, two schools in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He answered. I heard him say "oui" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry my answer is to be yes, but there is a problem with translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But neither showed up, "oui" or "yes" in English. But I heard distinctly heard the witness answer yes. So the answer to your first question was yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness Exhibit 272. It's a picture which is not on the CD-ROM. It's a photograph representing Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why don't we put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you scroll down. No, sorry. Can you move up a little, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that the old school was located alongside the road which led to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] At the edge not exactly, but, yes, very close to the road that goes towards Serbia through the so-called iron bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At any rate, it's much closer to the road than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Did it have a name, that old school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We know it under the acronym "old school" or "technical school", but we don't know the real name of this school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A while ago --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't you. Yes, it is approximately 15 metres away from the road you are mentioning, while the Vuk Karadzic school would be at 150 metres from that road, or 100 metres from that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a while ago Witness 42, and you said that you did not remember having questioned this witness. Let me remind you that on the 14th of September you stated that, as far as you remembered, this witness had been detained in the old school, at page 1442 of the 14th of September testimony.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might mix one of the two of the Branjevo survivors, but yes, for sure, one of the two says he was held in that location. And I think he was taken there on 13 and left on 15 July, in that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show the witness the statement made by Witness 42. This is Exhibit 3D15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it this is a Nikolic exhibit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Can we see the bottom of the page where we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is this your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now see page 3? Yes, page 3 of the statement, second paragraph. Second sentence in the second paragraph, the witness stated that: [In English] "They stopped in front of the school that looked abandoned and which is along the road in the direction of the Serbia." [Interpretation] Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that the description of the school and its location perfectly matched the old school, the technical school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we showed him the picture. So that was making sure of the situation, though -- though we didn't go and look for the petrol pump, nor did we for the church, and we didn't go and look for a sawmill in -- also. But, yes, the description is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Last sentence of that paragraph, paragraph 2, the witness stated: [In English] "I don't know the name of the school, but it is an old one. There is another school in Bratunac which is more recent." [Interpretation] Is it correct to say that at the time the witness was unable to give you the name of the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. He probably was speaking about the Vuk Karadzic school, but he didn't know the name of that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, did he mention the old school or the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll speak in English. He said that he was in one school and that there is a more recent one. So if we know that these two schools, one is named the old school and one, the Vuk Karadzic school, I bet that the most recent one is not the old one but the Vuk Karadzic school. And the one we know under the name of "old school" or "technical school" is the one that he recognised on a photograph. So this is why I believe that the other one he's referring to should be the Vuk Karadzic school, but he doesn't know the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: However, he was held in the old school, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 14th of September, you stated on page 1624 of the transcript, and I'm going to quote you in English: [In English] "The ultimate stage of an investigation is to present the evidence in a courtroom. In a courtroom we show the information that is the result of leads that we have followed and that we the Prosecutor leaves are positive." [Interpretation] I would like to know this: Did you listen to the

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My apologies to you, Madam Fauveau, but we needed to do that. Please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry, because I am the one who mentioned his testimony in the previous cases. However, now I can't remember whether the witness remembers my question, and if I have to put it again, we'll have to move to private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that this is interesting, because all the officials I have interviewed in Bratunac, all of them have made a lot of efforts in order to convince me that the Vuk Karadzic school had not been used at the time of these events. Only Mr. Deronjic backed off a little bit and conceded that one classroom had been used. And now today you tell us that, in fact, yes, the Vuk Karadzic school was apparently in full use, because not only one classroom was used according to that witness. So I must say that for me it's a discovery that we have a survivor from the Vuk Karadzic school. I mean, not from the Vuk Karadzic school complex but precisely from the Vuk Karadzic school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: No, no, this is not my theory. He was not held. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: (redacted)That was my theory, and I was asking you whether you could account for the fact that, at one point, the witness changed his statement as to the place of detention.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that this witness has changed his declaration. I just think that initially he said that he was in the so-called old school, because he refers to Vuk Karadzic without naming it as being a more recent one, and I bet that if he testified later on by saying "Vuk Karadzic school," it's because he believes that the old school has the name of Vuk Karadzic. That's the only explanation I can see here, at this stage anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Your opinion is that he was held in the old school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to move to another subject, the Petkovci school. On the 11th of September, transcript page 1493, you stated that you first identified the dam and then the school in Petkovci. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see my previous answer, "Yes, this is correct." At the previous question, there is nothing on the transcript. It's only written "[Previous translation continues] ..." But "Yes, this is correct" does not appear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing this out. My question was: Do you maintain that Witness 42 was detained in the old school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to move to another subject, the school in Petkovci. On the 11th of September, 2006, you said on page 1493 of the transcript, that you first identified the Petkovci dam and then the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you found the school, you took some photos of the school and you showed them to survivors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To one of them, yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Photo 158 of Exhibit 2103, could it be shown to the witness. Mr. President, you will notice that the CD-ROM that we received from the Prosecution has 262 photographs, but I think that up to there, it does -- it does match with the photos the Prosecutor showed us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have done my best --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have done my best to follow you, Madam Fauveau, but I was following in English and I don't think that the English interpretation is understandable as it is. It says: "Mr. President you will notice that the CD-ROM that we received from the Prosecution has 262 photographs, but I think that up to there, it does -- it does not match with the photos the Prosecutor showed us." If I understand you well, although it doesn't say so, is that before we were being shown a CD which, on the bottom of the monitor, it would show a total of 271, while here now we have a total of 262.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely the problem I was mentioning. We did not receive the CD-ROM that the Prosecutor showed us, but I think that here there is a perfect match with photo 258 of the Prosecutor's CD-ROM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 158. So basically, Mr. McCloskey and your case manager -- thank you for pointing that out, Madam Fauveau. Basically what Madam Fauveau wants confirmation of is that 158 of 262 would still be 158 of 271; in other words, that we are not referring to two different photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It should be. And to try to clear it up, we've given them two CDs, one with I think the lower number on it, and then when there is a few added we gave them another CD with that on it. So she's had both, but I think she's correct. It's the same -- the same school, the same photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you find out that it isn't, either of please, do let us know, for the record. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have received all the photos, there's no doubt about it, but we did not receive the CD-ROM with 271 photos on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is this the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that this photo was taken from the meadow that is in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. All right. Now it says so. Yes, go on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Mr. President, that the witness's answer to my last two questions was not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Initially it wasn't, and I got an explanation why it wasn't, but then, as you will see on line 15, "[Previous translation continues]..." that means there was overlapping. He did not allow sufficient time. But then there is "It is," which I take it is his answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was line 12. That's where the answer is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So it is -- yes. Let's go back through it. You were asked whether you recognised this as the Petkovci school and your answer was yes. And then you were asked whether it is correct to say that this photo was taken from the meadow which is in front of the school, and you answered yes as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, again, this shows the importance that you allow a little bit of a pause between Madam Fauveau's question and your answer, because I take it that you are following her in French.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's the reason why you are jumping, popping in straight with your answer in English before allowing for the interpreters to completely translate the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure you will. And we will have a break in six minutes' time, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It is correct to say that there's also a meadow in front of that school.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It is correct to say that the Rocevic school has a parking area at the back of the school.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a parking, a playground.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It may be a playground, but it was used also as a parking area, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for Rocevic school. My recollection is that on the picture one can see a playground, but the playground can indeed be used, if necessary, as a parking. And during these days I bet it was, in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated that the Petkovci school was a two-storey building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It is correct to say that the school in Grabovci also has two stories.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that the school in Rocevic is a two-storey building?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two floors. We count the ground floor as one floor. Are we on the same line on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The one in Pilica also has two floors.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to show you photo 165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we've fallen into the same problem again. We don't have in the transcript his translation. The one in Pilica also has two floors. Did you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he did put to you, Madam Fauveau, the statement that the ground floor would count as one floor. You agreed to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you, because I want to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: With regard to the school we see now in the screen, the school in Petkovci, the ground floor is a floor for you; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Indeed, it can be concluded that all these schools are two-storey buildings.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I count the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can photo 165 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You stated on the 11th of September, 2006, page 1496 of the transcript, that this shows the bullet hole in the blackboard.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you take that photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And did you find the bullet in the blackboard?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't search for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Therefore, you did not carry out any scientific analysis of the bullet hole or the bullet that would have been found?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing like that was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you find out during your investigation that the military soldiers of the VRS or the army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there is problem with the previous answer again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Indeed there is. You were asked --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is line 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You were asked, Mr. Ruez: "Therefore, you did not carry out any scientific analysis of the bullet hole or the bullet that would have been found?" And your answer was no, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer was no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you find out during your investigation that the military from the army of Republika Srpska would regularly come to the school in 1994 and also in spring 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We learned that, in fact, all the schools of the area were used from time to time as rest places for the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you learn during your investigation that fighting took place in the village around that school in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, not specifically on -- about this village, but the fact is that most of the places are indeed in former war zones, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could it not be that the bullet holes in the blackboard sort of date back to a period before the events of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is totally possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like the whole answer to be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Again, it's -- we only have the word "possible" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- as an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The full answer was: "It is totally possible."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Whenever it's convenient for you, Madam Fauveau, we can have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think it's a good time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will have a 30-minute break, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Fauveau, I take it that Mr. McCloskey would like to raise a couple of issues before you proceed with the cross-examination. Thank you for understanding. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very briefly, Mr. President, I just -- I was able to find the 30 August 2006 order from Judge Pocar regarding Ahmo Hasic, and we did, in fact, ask for both cases and he is cleared on both cases. So I don't know why I said to the contrary, but it's clear we can speak about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for that information. Thank you. No more issues to address? All right. So let's bring Mr. Ruez back in.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, on the 8th of September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. On the 8th --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry. I can't see the witness from where I stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How come you can't see the witness from where you stand? I can understand if you had a big column like we do -- oh, it's Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed. Mr. Ruez, we are going to proceed with Madam Fauveau's cross-examination of you. Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, on the 8th of September, 2006, you mentioned the Muslim population which was taken on buses to Kladanj and that then had to walk through the confrontation area. This was on the 8th of September, page 1332. Isn't it correct to say that during your investigation you discovered that this confrontation area was in fact an area which could be called a no-man's land?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. It was a no-man's land at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the Muslims, alongside with the Serbs, could organise the transportation in that area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the case because the area was mined on both sides. So on the Serbs -- and the Serb side took off -- took away their mines so the population could cross. The BiH army, as we can see on the film, advanced in that no-man's land up to the level of a tunnel, the tunnel being, in fact, the real physical separation between the two warring factions at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In other words, neither party could organise transportation in this area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the reason why the refugees could be seen on the film crossing this area on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, on that same day, the 8th of September, 2006, on the same page of the transcript, 1332, you said as follows: [In English] "The people who were bussed out of Srebrenica, they were taken towards this area, and from there they would walk by foot through the confrontation zone." [Interpretation] What I'm interested in is this: You discovered in the course of your investigation that people were put on the buses in Potocari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And, in fact, nobody was taken directly from Srebrenica to Kladanj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no direct transportation from Srebrenica. The collection point was Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 15th of September, 2006, on page 40 of the transcript, you talked about a Muslim man who had managed to get across to Muslim territory in Kladanj because he knew a soldier who was there. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we therefore conclude that the soldiers -- the soldier that was there had the power to decide who was going to move into Muslim territory and who wasn't?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say so. I don't believe they had the power to decide who would go or who would not go. But obviously one could have initiative to let someone go through, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As far as the man who took this initiative, you don't know whether he belonged to the army of Republika Srpska, the police in Zvornik, or the police in Bratunac, or whether he was a member of a paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, though we know what unit was on that location, though I do not remember this point precisely at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 12th of September, 2006, you commented on some pictures taken of two mosques, the mosque in Srebrenica and the mosque that was on the Zeleni Jadar road. Is it right to say that in your investigation you established that on the 13th of July, 1995, the Srebrenica mosque was still standing in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And as far as the Zeleni Jadar -- the mosque on the road to Zeleni Jadar, it was also established that it was still standing after the enclave in Srebrenica had been taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the following days, no; but the day General Mladic entered the town, yes, because this second mosque can be seen at a very precise moment during that film.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you have no information whereby this mosque was destroyed on the 12th, 13th, or 20th of --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not know the date of the start of the destruction, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: -- July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let me draw your attention again, and please do heed what I'm telling you, because I had a chat with the interpreters during the break: The fact that Madam Fauveau is addressing her questions in French, that you're listening in French and the way you are following up with questions and answers almost immediately is creating a lot of problems for them, especially because they were explaining to me how -- when you do this, how they need to, at least one section, wait for interpretation in English before they can then proceed with interpretation into B/C/S, and so on and so forth. So please do cooperate as much as you can. I know it's not easy. Sometimes I make the same mistake myself. But please do cooperate. Let's try and make the interpreters' job, which is already heavy and difficult, a little bit lighter. Thank you. And that brings me to line 15. I don't know whether, indeed, there was the full answer or whether there's only a part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The answer to the question at line 15 was that the investigation did not come up with any date that would signal the start of the destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ruez. Thank you, Madam Fauveau. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you, in the course of your investigation, discover when the mosque on the road to Zeleni Jadar had been built?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I shall now move on to the situation in Potocari. On the 15th of September, on page 31 of the transcript, you stated that the number of people who had assembled in Potocari amounted to 25.000 people, approximately. I wanted to ask you this question: Do you feel that this figure is right, i.e., 25.000 people?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that the number of people that reached Tuzla also amounted to 25.000 people, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We already talked about this issue related to the fact that these numbers cannot be accurate anyhow. I mean, if this intends to show that 25.000 people were at the departure and 25.000 at the arrival means that no one went missing in the process, this would be a wrong conclusion, since we know that an unknown number of men were among this group of roughly 25.000, but indeed we do not know how many of them have been separated and later killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it not right to say that the number of people that reached Tuzla only amounted to 4.900 -- 24.900?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Which means that there are a hundred people that are unaccounted for.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though the number at the arrival is precise, there was no count made at the departure, and there was even less of a count made of the men who were separated. So I don't buy at all your conclusion that 25.000, which is an unknown number, minus 24.900 could mean in any way that only 100 men were separated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you don't know how many men were in Potocari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered that. We can see on the pictures that were shown quite a number of faces that belonged to males, but no count of the male refugees was made at the -- at Potocari, at the exception of the list of approximately 240-something that was drafted by a member of the UN battalion who started that process at the beginning of the arrival of the refugees at the UN base, but this process was never completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of a document that comes from the ABiH army which mentions 300 fighters in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to talk about the purpose of your investigation. On the 12th of September, 2006, on page 1573 of the transcript, you stated: [In English] "What we quickly explained is that we would only be focusing in the first stage, the first stage that lasted very long, on mass execution." [Interpretation] I would like to know how much time the first phase of your investigation lasted.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This phase lasted approximately three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the second stage of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained previously, step one was creating a very precise, as precise as possible, picture of the main events. When saying "main events," I'm talking about the mass executions. And then step two was identification of units involved and perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 15th of September, 2006, on page 23 of the transcript, you talked about the UNHCR convoy, and you said: [In English] "Again, it has not been part of the investigation." [Interpretation] Is it right to say that your investigation did not focus on the treatment which the people in Potocari received?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. It did focus on the treatment of the people in Potocari. Though this aspect of the UNHCR convoy was indeed certainly not the focus of the investigation, we know enough about this convoy. The head of this convoy has been met by a member of the investigation team, and what we know about it is that the material that was brought in by the UN in order to ease the suffering of the refugees never reached the refugees. So that is, indeed, an aspect that was under investigation, though it was not at all the focus of -- as an important aspect of the treatment received by these refugees during these two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that your investigation did not look into the root causes of the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is totally right --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: -- the combat in Srebrenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not all the focus of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, you're moving too fast. Please, when you started answering the question, we were still halfway through the interpretation process.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The best would be that I get the same as you all have so that I could realise when the translation is over, because I don't have it in the earphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are following in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will do the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I think that will be better. Just move to channel 4 and that's all. Thanks. Now, that should solve the problem now, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was also my fault, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Maybe I shall repeat my last question. Is it right to say that your investigation did not focus on the root causes of the military operation in Srebrenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is totally right. The events between 1992 and 1995 in this area were not at all the topic of this investigation that was limited to investigate criminal events that followed the fall of the Srebrenica enclave, the reason why I often used to say the investigation starts on events beginning the 11 July, early afternoon, not before that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And therefore you did not investigate on the situation in Srebrenica before the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, though I came across information in connection with events from 1992 through 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: As your investigation started, as you said just now, on the 11th of July, in the beginning of the afternoon, you did not investigate on the reasons why the population of Srebrenica fled to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, this is so close to the 11th, around noon, that yes, indeed this was part of the investigation, since every single witness we interviewed did give a piece of information related to the reason why he made the choice to flee Srebrenica either to join Potocari or to join the group that was -- that intended to cross the lines by walking through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that this information was not really the focus of your interest?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is part of the surrounding events that lead later to a situation that is the topic of the investigation, and this situation is a large number of prisoners being under the control of the Bosnian Serb army and trying to find out what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity during your investigation to meet the people who, in 1995, were the military and political figure heads in Srebrenica? What I mean are the Muslim authorities.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met a few of them indeed, yes, in the course of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you give me their names, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on top of my memory. One of them was, in bracket, the mayor during the period of the siege, but I don't have his name in my head. Another one is Dr. Pilav, I think. Do you want to know the topic of these encounters?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In respect of the number of missing, the usual base that we are using is the ICRC list of missing people. The problem is that we believe that this list is incomplete, since entire families vanished. An example of it could be the Nuhanovic family. The father was a negotiator. He --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is something you've explained already.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I believe --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he is the only survivor of this family because he had a UN card, since he was an interpreter for the UN battalion. Had he fled through the woods, the entire family would have vanished and they would not have been on the missing list. Therefore, the initial contacts made in 1995 with the civilian representatives of the refugees in Srebrenica came up with the idea of drafting their own list by going through all the refugee centres, and they ended up with a list of 10.500 that we started to collect and tried to check. But then two years after they had started the process, they totally abandoned it because, in fact, they were facing a lot of criticism from the community of refugees. So that was the reason why I was in contact with these Muslim civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Among the people who were in the list of the Red Cross -- no, no, I'll move to another question. Strike that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Exhibit 5D19 be shown to the witness. We have it in our system but only the B/C/S. But we obtained the translation this morning, translation into English this morning. I have some copies for the witness and of course for the Trial Chamber. This is a newspaper article published in a Bosnian newspaper on the 2nd of March, 2000. I need page 6 of the English version; in Serbo-Croat, it is page 3, last column. It's the passage in the middle, in bold.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the translation into English of this newspaper article?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Registrar, I know that the -- Madam Usher, that the B/C/S version, the original, is on, but perhaps it would also help the public if we put the English version, page 6, on the ELMO, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [In English] So it's the last paragraph, and it starts in the middle of the last paragraph. In this paragraph you can read this: "The greatest surprise at the Assembly was experienced by Hakija Meholic, the president of the Srebrenica SDP, Social Democratic Party. "They drove us in armoured personnel carriers from the airport to the Holiday Inn. There we were met by President Izetbegovic, and after greeting us he immediately asked: 'What do you think about exchanging Srebrenica for Vogosca?' There was silence for a while, and then I spoke up and said: 'Mr. President, if you brought us here for a fait accompli, then you shouldn't have done that because we have to return to our people...' Then he said: 'You know, in April 1993, Clinton made me an offer if the Chetnik forces enter Srebrenica and massacre 5.000 Muslims, then there will be military intervention.' Our delegation consisted of nine people, including one from Bratunac who, sadly, is the only one who is no longer alive..." [Interpretation] Sir, I would like to know whether you heard of this offer made by President Clinton to President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the 2nd of March, 2000, you were still employed with the OTP, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Nobody told you that Mr. Hakija Meholic would have made such a statement regarding this fact?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: So you did not investigate into this fact.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I known about it, I would anyhow not have investigated about it. This is part of the political surroundings. This investigation was not investigating the political aspect of this situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But is this not a piece of information that sheds a totally different light on the events in Srebrenica in July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is that during at least five years, so-called theories of conspiracy were flying in all directions that many journalists have followed leads in order to investigate the political aspect of all this. And these theories of conspiracy have never been the topic of the investigation I was in charge of. I would have read this, heard this, but taken no action in terms of investigation about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware if Hakija Meholic was ever interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor, and whether he released any statements, for that matter, whether he has testified in other proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know in general for the OTP, but he was not interviewed in the frame of the Srebrenica 1995 investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you know that Hakija Meholic was the chief of police in July 1995 in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Exhibit 5D27 be shown to the witness. It is a newspaper article published in Le Monde, a French newspaper, on the 24th of February, 2001. I would need the second page, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
